_about.credit: The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The database was created with funding from NSF EIA-0196217.
_about.rig: human.py (27 bones), reference man human.build(seed=0, stand=0.02, curl=(30, 45, 25)), 1.75 m
_about.frame: Blender's: x forward, y LEFT, z up, metres. For Unreal's y-right frame mirror quaternions as (w, -x, y, -z) and locations as (x, -y, z).
_about.bones: per bone, per frame, [w, x, y, z]: the rotation D relative to the bone's rest, in its PARENT's space (the bone's local rotation in its parent's frame = D * RestLocal). Blender pose quaternion = RestLocal^-1 * D * RestLocal.
_about.pelvis_loc: per frame [x, y, z]: the pelvis head's offset from its rest place, in the armature's space. The root bone never moves (IN PLACE). Scale it by (this man's leg / leg) for another man.
_about.loops: frames includes the closing frame, equal to the first: length = (frames - 1) / fps. Play rate for a travel loop = speed / stride * length (stride: metres travelled per loop by this 1.75 m man).

walk.note: Subject 35, plain walk. One full two-step cycle.

run.note: Subject 35, run/jog: the same man as the walk.

idle.note: Subject 77 (careful actions), standing: weight shifts, a glance about.

march.note: Subject 21, 'soldiers march': a parade march with straight arms swung to the shoulder.

advance.note: The run (35_18) with a crouch laid over it: pelvis 14 cm lower, trunk 28 degrees further forward, head kept up, knees bent by IK on the captured foot paths (CMU's own careful runs, 77_10-13, are short bursts and circles that do not loop).

creep.note: Subject 136, 'walk crouched': knees bent, trunk forward, a careful crouched walk.

get_up.note: Subject 77: from lying on the belly, push up, a knee forward, up into a careful ready crouch.

go_prone.note: get_up's first 2.7 s played backwards and 1.4x faster: from the ready crouch down onto a knee, the hands, and flat on the belly. Its last frame is get_up's first, so the two chain exactly.

fall_forward.note: 140_01's get-up from face down, played backwards: a jolt at the hit (the trunk snaps forward, the head lags), the knees buckle and he drops at up to 4.4x (the fall about 1.8x faster than a plain 2.1x reversal), the arms only half catching him (part way to slack), then he settles at real speed. CMU has no shot-and-collapse take.

fall_back.note: Subject 90, 'rug pull fall', with a jolt at the hit (the trunk snaps back, the head lags): the feet go from under him and he lands on his back, in real time (about half a second from the feet going to the ground). The actor fell onto a mat, sank into it and bounced; ours is eased down in the fall and stays on the ground.

stumble.note: Subject 77, 'limping, hurt right leg': bent over, a quick step on the good leg.

cower.note: Subject 79, 'scared': hunched, hands up by the face.

duck.note: Subject 77, 'duck to avoid flying object': drops into a crouch with the head down, then rises.

crawl.source: keyed by hand on the rig (no capture)
crawl.note: Keyed by hand (CMU has no belly crawl): the low crawl under fire. Chest and hips on the ground, the head low, the rifle across the forearms in the right hand; one elbow and the same side's knee draw up together, side by side in turn; elbows and knees planted while they pull. 0.40 m a loop.

crawl_high.note: Subject 111, crawling on hands and knees (a woman, pregnant: the only clean crawl in the library), for moving behind low cover. She slid her hands along the floor; ours are planted and step (hand_steps), each with the other side's knee.
